samples.summary: Blame labels are recomputed with a full O(runs) CRDT walk plus an O(lines × runs) scan on every document change, and the run count grows monotonically with every edit ever made to the note
samples.evidence: `NoteBlameTracker.update()` calls `this.store.getAuthorSpans()` on every `docChanged` update. `YorkieNoteStore.getAuthorSpans()` (yorkie-note-store.ts:158-186) iterates every node of `root.content.values()` and allocates a fresh span object per node. Because `editText` now attaches `{a, t}` with a fresh `Date.now()` to every insertion (yorkie-note-store.ts:145-151), adjacent inserts never share attributes, so the node/span count grows roughly with the number of keystrokes ever made in the note and never shrinks. `computeBlameLabels` then calls `authorOfRange` per line, and `authorOfRange` rescans the span array from index 0 each time (`for (const span of spans) { if (span.to <= from) continue; ... }`, blame-gutter.ts:44-50) — O(lines × spans). On a long-lived note (say 10k historical edits, 500 lines) that is millions of comparisons plus 10k object allocations per keystroke, on the synchronous typing path. MemNoteStore is worse in constant factor: `getAuthorSpans()` (memory.ts:100-122) loops per character of the whole document. No incremental/cached path exists.

samples.summary: The last line of a document is never attributed when it is empty — the empty-line rule the code documents does not apply at end of document
samples.evidence: `const to = line.to > line.from ? line.to : Math.min(line.from + 1, doc.length);` For a trailing empty line, `line.from === line.to === doc.length`, so `Math.min(line.from + 1, doc.length) === line.from` and the range passed to `authorOfRange` is empty → `best` stays null → blank label. So the extremely common case (user presses Enter at the end of the note and is sitting on the new empty last line) shows no author, while an identical empty line in the middle of the document is attributed to whoever typed its newline (covered by the test at blame-gutter.test.ts 'attributes an empty line to whoever typed the newline ending it'). The behaviour is inconsistent and untested for the end-of-doc case.

samples.summary: `span.at >= best.at` tie-break lets a later unattributed run blank out a line that has a genuine author
samples.evidence: `if (!best || span.at >= best.at) best = span;` — unattributed runs report `at: 0` and so do attributed runs whose timestamp was rejected by `sanitizeWrittenAt` (non-number, missing `t`, or a future `t`; yorkie-note-store.ts:66-72). When a line contains an attributed run with `at === 0` followed in document order by a legacy/unattributed run (`author: null, at: 0`), the `>=` makes the null run win and `authorOfRange` returns null, so the line renders blank even though a real author is recorded on it. The comment claims `at: 0` means 'any real edit outranks them', which is only true for runs whose timestamp survived sanitisation.

samples.summary: `sanitizeDisplayName` truncates after stripping lone surrogates, so the truncation itself can re-introduce a lone surrogate into the DOM
samples.evidence: The pipeline is `.replace(INVISIBLE_RE, '').replace(UNICODE_SPACE_RE, ' ').slice(0, MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_LENGTH).trim()`. `INVISIBLE_RE` includes `\p{Cs}` and runs BEFORE `slice`. `String.prototype.slice` cuts at a UTF-16 code-unit boundary, so a name whose 64th/65th code units are a surrogate pair (e.g. an emoji or an astral-plane script at the cap) is cut in half, leaving an unpaired surrogate in the returned string. That value is then written straight into `span.textContent` (blame-gutter.ts:112), `span.title` (blame-gutter.ts:118) and the caret label (remote-selection.ts:67), and in the Yorkie store it is also written back into the CRDT attribute (yorkie-note-store.ts:149). Stripping should happen after the length cap, or the cap should be code-point aware.

samples.summary: `MemNoteStore.splice` spreads an array of one element per inserted character into `Array.prototype.splice`, which throws RangeError for large inserts
samples.evidence: `this.authors.splice(from, to - from, ...new Array<MemAuthorMark>(insert.length).fill(mark));` The spread becomes one argument per inserted character. Pasting a document of ~100k characters into a MemNoteStore-backed editor (the in-package dev store, also used by every engine test and by `initialize` in non-collaborative use) exceeds the engine's argument limit and throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` from inside `editText`, aborting the edit mid-way — `this.text` has already been updated on the previous line (memory.ts:126), so the store is left with `text` and `authors` out of sync (authorship silently misaligned for the rest of the document).

samples.summary: The gutter renders one frame with labels bound to the pre-edit line numbering, so labels visibly attach to the wrong lines until the microtask repaint lands
samples.evidence: `lineMarkerChange` only returns true for the tracker's `blameRepaint` annotation, and the gutter plugin is registered before `basicSetup` — i.e. earlier in the extension order than `noteBlameTracker` — so during a doc-changing update the gutter re-renders reading the WeakMap entry the tracker has not yet replaced (`labelsByView`, blame-gutter.ts:98). The tracker only publishes afterwards and then schedules the corrective repaint via `queueMicrotask` (blame-gutter.ts:173-181). For a change that inserts or removes lines (Enter, paste, a remote edit) every label below the change point is drawn against the wrong line for that frame. The same stale-index path is what the code hits permanently if the store's text ever diverges from the CM doc (e.g. a dispatch whose userEvent is not in `NoteSyncPluginValue.EDIT_EVENTS`, note-sync.ts:55, never reaches the store) — spans are then in a different coordinate space than `doc` and labels misalign silently rather than blanking.

samples.summary: The persisted `showAuthors` preference is not applied to the shared-document note mount, so the toggle silently has no effect there
samples.evidence: `<NotesView readOnly={readOnly} viewMode={readOnly ? "view" : "both"} />` — `showAuthors` is not passed, so `NotesView` falls back to its `showAuthors = false` default (notes-view.tsx:85) and `readShowAuthors()` is never consulted on this path. A user who turns 'Show authors' on in /notes and then opens the same note through a share link (including an editable share, where they will be writing attribution into the CRDT) gets no gutter and no way to enable one. Every other persisted note preference is read from `notes-settings.ts` at the owning host; this one is only read in `notes-detail.tsx`.
searchedFor: grep readShowAuthors / writeShowAuthors across the repo

samples.summary: Every blame repaint dispatch also drives the remote-selection plugin, which republishes local presence through a Yorkie `doc.update`
samples.evidence: `view.dispatch({ annotations: [blameRepaint.of(true)] })` is an ordinary transaction, so `NoteRemoteSelectionsPluginValue.update` runs for it and unconditionally calls `this.store.setLocalSelection(...)` (remote-selection.ts:110-119), which in `YorkieNoteStore` opens a `doc.update` (yorkie-note-store.ts:418). With the gutter enabled that is one extra Yorkie update per label-changing keystroke. It is deduplicated by the JSON comparison at yorkie-note-store.ts:408 so no presence change is actually pushed, but the extra update/transaction cycle per keystroke is unnecessary work that the annotation could have been used to skip.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: NoteBlameTracker.update() recomputes labels from this.store.getAuthorSpans() on every docChanged (blame-gutter.ts:145-154), computeBlameLabels calls authorOfRange per line (blame-gutter.ts:71-79), authorOfRange rescans the span array from index 0 (blame-gutter.ts:44-50, with an early `break` at :46 bounding each scan), YorkieNoteStore.getAuthorSpans() allocates a span plus a sanitizeDisplayName regex pass per CRDT node (yorkie-note-store.ts:158-186, display-name.ts:31-57), editText stamps a fresh Date.now() per insertion (yorkie-note-store.ts:144-151), and MemNoteStore.getAuthorSpans() loops per character (memory.ts:100-122). No cache or incremental path exists. However the asserted defect is purely cost/scalability: the computed labels are correct, and there is no wrong condition, boundary error, null-guard crash, async/ordering mistake, swallowed error, retained resource, or broken invariant — so it falls outside the Correctness lane (logic and runtime correctness), belonging to a performance lens instead. Supporting containment: the gutter and tracker are compartment-gated behind the opt-in showAuthors flag (editor.ts:356, 388, 517-526), authorOfRange breaks early (blame-gutter.ts:46), and update() skips repaint when labels are unchanged (blame-gutter.ts:151), so it degrades responsiveness at scale rather than crashing or breaking a flow. Refuting on scope only; the facts stand for a performance reviewer.
